solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Provisions to go south to be moved to end in police observation

indicators.note: the clue says the letter for south must be shifted to the final position of the surveillance word

parts.note: a stakeout is police watching a place in secret

explanation.surface: Supplies for a police surveillance team are shifted south to the end of the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals bought to eat elsewhere are food provisions you carry off, a plural noun matching the clue.

clue.text: Marks on skin from grot, moreover

parts.note: grot is British slang for junk or rubbish, as is tat
too means also or moreover

explanation.surface: Someone complains that ink markings on the body come from grubby stuff, and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: GROT and TAT are both British slang for shoddy, worthless stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a verb, to ink a design permanently into someone is to mark their skin.

clue.text: European absorbed by religious text's language

indicators.note: something absorbed by another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: the Koran is the holy book of Islam

explanation.surface: A European soaks up the language of a holy scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of North and South Korea is a language.

clue.text: Bats, ernes and owls not under control

indicators.note: bats as an adjective means crazy, so the following letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of flying creatures — bats, sea eagles and owls — none of them tamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the first creature in the list, but it is the anagram signal meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no keeper or proprietor is free of anyone's control, as with a stray animal.

clue.text: Solver scrapes nose

parts.note: scrapes, in the sense of awkward predicaments, are troubles
hooter is British slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A crossword solver scratches their nose in concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: A person brought in to fix problems is a solver of difficulties, a fixer.

clue.text: King has initially ignored expression of disgust for fortress

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word has is left out

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: A monarch has, at first, brushed off a grunt of disgust aimed at his stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African citadel, or the old quarter around it, is a fortified place.

clue.text: Party in upcoming period to enjoy

indicators.note: the party word sits inside the period word
in a down clue, upcoming means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party in the coming season is something to look forward to enjoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns ERA to ARE, which then holds DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To love something greatly is to delight in it, a stronger synonym for enjoy.

clue.text: Turned up carrying gold in chief shipping route

indicators.note: the inner group of letters sits within the chief word

parts.note: a boss is a chief

indicators.note: the turned word carries the gold inside it
turned means the following word is flipped round

parts.note: taken as written
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A cargo of gold turns up in a major shipping lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as one phrase meaning arrived, but 'Turned' alone acts on 'up', giving PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The strait at Istanbul linking the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara is a major passage for ships.

clue.text: Greek's anguish with opponents in charge

parts.note: hell is extreme torment or anguish
E and N, East and North, are opposing partnerships at bridge

explanation.surface: A Greek's agony when his rivals hold power.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things relating to ancient or modern Greece, from Hellas, its native name.

clue.text: Publication is all crime, a flexible literary genre

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

indicators.note: flexible means the letters can be bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A magazine that prints nothing but crime fiction belongs to a loose, adaptable genre.
explanation.definitionFit: The style of fiction, linked with García Márquez, that sets fantastical events in an everyday world is a literary genre.

clue.text: Big city companion to homesick girl crosses river — no going back

indicators.note: the companion's name spans the other letters, holding them within

parts.note: Toto is the dog of Dorothy, who longs for home in The Wizard of Oz

indicators.note: going back means the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: A homesick girl's companion crosses a river on a journey that cannot be retraced.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz famously says 'There's no place like home'. 'going back' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ontario is Canada's largest metropolis, a big city.

clue.text: Love powerful nation in a sport bringing excitement

indicators.note: the love and nation letters go inside the other pair

parts.note: RL is the abbreviation for rugby league
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
the USA is a superpower

explanation.surface: Passion for a mighty country's game makes for thrilling times.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred up or roused is a state of excitement, often of a sexual kind.

clue.text: Live roughly in a row, with the last being detached

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of the phrase is cut off before the rest is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lives rough in a line of houses, with the end one standing apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping W leaves INARO, which 'roughly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast going out live is being transmitted at that moment, a broadcasting idiom.

clue.text: British free alien, with honour intended

parts.note: to rid is to free
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film
an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A British alien is set free and given an honour, as was always planned.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Intended' as a noun is a fiancé or fiancée, so a woman soon to marry fits.

clue.text: Japanese mash-up of Queen and Oasis with one special ingredient

indicators.note: a mash-up blends songs together, so the words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Japanese DJ remixes Queen and Oasis tracks, adding one special element.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for an indefinable quality is an elusive special something that makes a thing distinctive.

clue.text: Flatter track possesses little gradient, ultimately

indicators.note: the track word possesses, that is holds within it, the other letters

parts.note: to stalk is to track
wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of gradient

explanation.surface: A flatter running track has only a slight incline at its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative adjective describing the track, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone with charming words and compliments is to flatter them.

clue.text: Happy to be docked pound after upset father's pacified

indicators.note: the docked word comes after the father word
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: docked means having something cut off, here the pound letter

parts.note: pleased means happy
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man is glad to lose some money once his upset dad has been calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PA to AP; PLEASED 'docked' of L gives PEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone calmed by having their demands met has been soothed or placated.

clue.text: Reference works by venerated people supporting learner with English

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate
x means by, as in a room's dimensions, 3 x 4
icons are revered figures

explanation.surface: Reference books written by revered figures help a learner with English.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries and word lists are reference works.

clue.text: Journalists rush son to make accusation

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively
to charge is to rush forward

explanation.surface: Reporters hurry a man's son off so they can level an allegation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a formal legal complaint against someone is to make an accusation.

clue.text: Charm about Italian cocktail

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the charm word goes round the other

parts.note: mojo is a magic charm or personal magnetism

explanation.surface: An Italian's charm works round a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban drink of rum, mint, lime and soda is a cocktail.

clue.text: Reasonable day to replace contemporary's leader

indicators.note: the day letter takes the place of another letter
leader points at the opening letter of the contemporary word

parts.note: recent means contemporary or modern

explanation.surface: A sensible day stands in for the boss of a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable or fair, as in a decent wage, means reasonable.

clue.text: Author from east, distance unknown, vacated oriental area

parts.note: a mile is a distance
z is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A writer from the east has travelled a vague distance away from an empty eastern region.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist of Germinal and J'accuse is an author.

clue.text: Semi-firm board

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the business word is kept

parts.note: an enterprise is a firm or business

explanation.surface: A board of medium firmness, like a mattress or panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-firm' reads as a description of the board, but 'board' is the verb meaning get on.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a train or ship is to go into it.

clue.text: Valuable collection is the last in art range

indicators.note: the last in picks the final letter of art

parts.note: to range is to rove or wander

explanation.surface: A prized art collection is the latest in a gallery's range.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard of treasure or valuable finds is a precious collection.

clue.text: Sally hugging Henry's little one

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the sally word encloses the other letter

parts.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden military outing
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally cuddles Henry's small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name, but it is a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a short person or small child, a little one.

clue.text: Fancy a drink, with one compiler getting round?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: getting round means surrounding, so the compiler word goes round the other letters

parts.note: the compiler, the setter, refers to themself as me
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Fancy a drink? One crossword setter is buying a round.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy, as in suppose or picture, is to conceive in the mind.

clue.text: What we want of French father

parts.note: de is French for of
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A question of what we want from a French father.
explanation.definitionFit: A longing or wish is a want, the feeling behind what we want.

clue.text: Attempt to oust pesky mouse, spanning fair time

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the rearranged letters straddle the fair word
pesky means troublesome, so the letters misbehave and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
OK means fair or satisfactory

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get rid of an annoying mouse over a reasonable period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pesky' seems merely to describe the rodent, yet it signals the rearrangement to SMEOU.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone out of hiding with smoke, or by other pressure, is an attempt to oust them.
